status: Method rationale before new experiment labels; no accuracy claim

primary_sources.title: LLVM KnownBits reference
primary_sources.supports: Known-zero/known-one arithmetic analysis includes addition with carry and addition/subtraction transfer functions.

primary_sources.title: LLVM GlobalISel Known Bits Analysis
primary_sources.supports: Known-bits information is used in compiler analysis and optimization.

local_hypothesis: Retaining sound known-bit information through ADD/ADDI may distinguish narrow shifted data plus constants from unconstrained wide arithmetic, improving localized circuit descriptors. This must be tested using matched fitting and fresh synthesis labels.
implementation_derivation: For each bit, enumerate the possible operand bits and incoming carry. Mark an output bit known only if every combination agrees; propagate the set of possible outgoing carries. Start with carry zero and discard carry beyond bit31 for RV32 modular addition. Ignoring correlations overapproximates possibilities rather than inventing known bits.
validation_required: Exhaustive small-width abstract/concrete tests plus RV32 boundary, overflow, negative-immediate, shared-input and nested-expression checks; unchanged old feature outputs. Feature precision alone is not evidence of LUT accuracy or safe budget classification.
novelty_boundary: Known-bits arithmetic is established compiler analysis, not claimed as a new invention. Our transfer routine is an independently implemented conservative recurrence; no LLVM dependency or copied implementation is introduced.
comparison_boundary: Two matched fits can isolate the added descriptors on identical rows; they do not separately identify causal effects of the simultaneous new training coverage and policy change.
